location.basis: Published coordinates 30°37′44″N 72°51′50″E (English Wikipedia, Harappa). Not checked against imagery: plan-B works from published plans only.

sources.citation_or_service: Vats, M. S. 1940. Excavations at Harappa, vol. II (plates). Delhi: Manager of Publications. Plate III, 'Harappa Mound F: Plan of the Great Granary Area and Section on A.B.'

north_arrow_measurement.method: fitted to 245 ink pixels within 3.0 px (RMS 0.54 px)
north_arrow_measurement.description: Ruled arrow about 145 px long pointing to the left of the page, with a short cross-bar and the letter N at its head; fitted to the shaft.

rendering_check.note: Checked on the plan's printed site grid. The horizontal grid lines turn progressively from 0.0 deg at the top of the sheet to -0.7 deg at the bottom and the vertical lines fan by up to 0.65 deg towards the right edge, so the fold-out was photographed slightly out of plane. Between the arrow (bottom right) and the granary (centre) the local rotation differs by about 0.3 deg; we take 0.4 deg.

sources.notes: The plan is printed with north to the left of the page.

sources.citation_or_service: Wheeler, R. E. M. 1947. Harappa 1946: the defences and Cemetery R 37. Ancient India 3: 58-130. Plate XV, 'Harappa 1946. The Citadel (Mound AB) and Cemeteries'.
sources.north_label_text: (compass rose with an arrowhead on the north spoke; no letter legible at this resolution)
sources.scale_bar: Scale of Feet 50 0 100 200 300 400 500 600; Scale of Metres

north_arrow_measurement.description: Eight-pointed compass rose in a double circle, about 135 px from the arrowhead to the foot of the north-south spindle. We took the midline of the spindle above and below the circle from the pixel profiles.

rendering_check.note: The plate has a ruled border but it is cut off on the left of the scan, and the sheet is torn across the north end of the citadel. With no usable frame pair we assume 0.5 deg for shear and curvature of this folded, torn plate.

sources.notes: Article PDF from the Internet Archive item harappa1946.

systems.description: The two long walls of the granary blocks, the sleeper walls of the halls and the retaining wall

systems.part: Citadel (Mound AB), east and west walls

main_system_reason: The Great Granary on Mound F is the most regular rectilinear building at Harappa and its long walls are the straightest measured lines on any of the plans; the citadel walls form a parallelogram whose long sides and south side do not share one direction, so they cannot stand for a single layout.
notes: We measured Vats's plan of the Great Granary area on Mound F (1940, Plate III) and Wheeler's plan of the citadel, Mound AB (1947, Plate XV). Neither arrow says what kind of north it is. On Vats's plan the two long walls of the granary blocks and the sleeper walls of the halls agree within about one degree; the plan is printed with north to the left and carries the site grid, which we used to check the distortion of the fold-out. Wheeler's citadel is a parallelogram: its east and west walls share one direction, about twelve degrees off the plan's north, while its south wall runs almost due east-west on the same plan. The plate is a 100 dpi scan of a torn fold-out and its north is a decorative compass rose, so its errors are larger. The two plans cover different mounds and their north arrows were drawn independently, so their systems are reported separately. The lower town (Mound E and ET) and the HARP plans were not measured.
